headlines.title: What Is Ross Stores (ROST) Telling Investors With UBS's Upgrade?
headlines.summary: Ross Stores (NasdaqGS:ROST) was upgraded to "buy" by UBS, citing the retailer's growth potential under new CEO Jim Conroy. UBS highlighted Conroy's focus on narrowing the store productivity gap between Ross locations and key off-price competitors. The broker's commentary pointed to operational changes at Ross Stores that aim to improve in-store efficiency and shopper throughput.

headlines.title: Ross Stores upgraded by UBS as store productivity gap offers growth potential
headlines.summary: UBS has upgraded Ross Stores Inc (NASDAQ:ROST), the US discount retailer, to 'buy' from 'neutral' and raised its price target by 32% to $315, forecasting 37% upside as improving store productivity drives earnings growth.

headlines.title: Ross Stores climbs as UBS upgrades shares to Buy on stronger sales outlook
headlines.summary: Investing.com -- UBS upgraded Ross Stores to Buy from Neutral and raised its price target to $315 from $239, saying the off-price retailer’s recent same-store sales momentum can persist beyond this year and drive meaningful upward earnings revisions.

description: Ross Stores, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates off-price retail apparel and home fashion stores under the Ross Dress for Less and dd's DISCOUNTS brands in the United States. The company offers designer apparel, accessories, footwear, and home-fashioned products for the entire family. It sells its products to middle income households and households with lower to more moderate incomes. Ross Stores, Inc. was incorporated in 1957 and is headquartered in Dublin, California.
